# M2 · Basis Anatomy: results

**Run:** 23 Oct 2026 on the M1 snapshot (futures through 22 Oct 2026). Every number below comes from `m2_tables.md`, regenerated by `python "PS Research/m2_basis/summarise_m2.py"`. The method is in `tola/anatomy.py`; the outputs are `data/snapshot/basis_daily.parquet` (27,225 contract-days) and `curve_daily.parquet` (1,850 days).

## What the anatomy does

For every traded contract and day, the futures price per gram (999) is split into four terms. All are in bp against the same day's Ahmedabad 999 polled spot, and they add up exactly:

| Step | What it measures | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | Lot, quote unit and purity | Done in M1 (`close_g999`). GOLD and GOLDM are lifted by 999/995. |
| **Timing** | Spot is polled around 5–6 pm; the futures close is the last half hour to about 11:30 pm | Intercept of the day's benchmark curve. It is common to every contract that day. |
| **Carry** | Time to settlement | Slope of the day's benchmark curve (GOLD and GOLDM, ₹1 Cr+ turnover, outside tender) × time to the contract's effective settlement date. GOLD and GOLDM settle on a 3-day average, so their settlement date sits about a day earlier; that is how "single poll vs 3-day average" enters. |
| **Reference** | Which spot the contract settles to | Own polled spot vs Ahmedabad 999. Non-zero only for GOLDPETAL (Mumbai). |
| **Residual** | Whatever is left | The small-lot premium, if any |

**Delivery terms are shown, not subtracted.** The making charge, delivery unit and tender margin sit next to the residual. The buyer pays the making charge *on top of* the settlement price the futures converge to, so it is not part of the futures price by construction. The data agrees (finding 3).

## Findings

**1. Gold futures carried below the risk-free rate for five years, then far above it.**

| | Implied carry | Risk-free | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2020–2024 | 1.5–4.0% | 4.0–6.5% (repo) | **−1.4 to −2.8 pp every year** |
| 2025 | 5.6% | 5.5% | about 0 |
| 2026 so far | 12.3% | 5.3% (FBIL 3M T-bill) | **+7 pp** |

Month by month, the jump starts in **Oct 2025** (6.7%) and peaks in **Jan 2026** (17.2%). It stays at **11–15% until Jun 2026**, then eases to **7–10% from Jul 2026**. For eight months, buyers paid 5–12 pp a year over T-bills to hold gold for later delivery. That is the bullion boom showing up in the curve. The fit stays tight (median rmse 9–20 bp) except in Jan–Feb 2026 (34–38 bp), around the 30 Jan crash.

**2. The timing term is large, so it has to be stripped first.** Half of all days sit between about −50 and +50 bp; one day in five is beyond ±85 bp. This is gold moving between the spot poll and the futures close. It hits every contract equally. Without it, every "basis to spot" number is mostly noise. The 2020 90th percentile (+1,090 bp) comes from the lockdown, when the polled spot was frozen for 49 days.

**3. The making charge is not priced into the futures.** 2025–26 medians:

| Contract | Residual | Making charge |
|---|---|---|
| GOLDTEN | **+2.5 bp** | ₹30/g ≈ 21 bp |
| GOLDGUINEA | +66 bp | ₹25/g ≈ 18 bp |
| GOLDPETAL | +85 bp | ₹100/g ≈ 70 bp |
| GOLD, GOLDM (benchmark) | −1.8 / +2.4 bp | none |

GOLDTEN carries a making charge and sits flat on the big-lot curve. GOLDGUINEA's charge is *smaller* than GOLDTEN's per gram, yet its residual is 64 bp larger. So the small-lot premium is not the making charge. GOLDPETAL's charge comes close to its residual, but the GOLDTEN and GOLDGUINEA evidence says not to read that as cause.

**4. The residual is the small-lot premium, and it has a history.**

| Year | GOLDGUINEA | GOLDPETAL |
|---|---|---|
| 2020 | +32 | +32 |
| 2021 | +12 | −50 |
| 2022 | −24 | −70 |
| 2023 | +35 | −91 |
| 2024 | +74 | **−144** |
| 2025 | +54 | **+76** |
| 2026 | +77 | +94 |

GOLDGUINEA has traded above the big-lot curve in most years. GOLDPETAL traded at a widening *discount* from 2021 to 2024, then flipped to a premium in 2025. That is the regime break G0 noted. M1 also found that GOLDPETAL closed 125–255 bp below its own settlement price at expiry in late 2023 and 2024. Both point to the pre-2025 GOLDPETAL contract as different in kind (S1).

**5. The Mumbai reference is small.** GOLDPETAL's own spot (Mumbai) runs **1–8 bp below** Ahmedabad 999 (median by year). It explains almost none of GOLDPETAL's residual in any year.

## What this means for the build

- **M3 (convergence monitor)** should compare GOLDTEN, GOLDGUINEA and GOLDPETAL on the *residual* and on same-expiry ratios. Comparing raw basis to spot carries ±50–85 bp of timing noise.
- **M4 (walk-forward):** carry is not stable (17% in Jan 2026, 7% in Jul 2026), so any rule must use the day's fitted carry, never a constant.
- **M5 (chooser):** the making charge belongs in the "take delivery" cost and nowhere else. The evidence that it isn't priced into the futures is finding 3.
- **The app's Basis page** can draw the waterfall straight from `basis_daily`: unit → spot → timing → carry → reference → residual, with `fair_g999` as the "fair price" marker.

## Limits

- **Risk-free before Oct 2025 is the RBI repo rate**, not a T-bill. FBIL's public endpoint serves only 12 months; our cache now holds Oct 2025 onward and grows with each refresh. The 91-day bill usually trades within about 0.5 pp of repo, so the 2020–24 gap is too large to be a proxy artefact.
- **The benchmark curve is a straight line in time to settlement.** On stressed days (41 days with rmse > 40 bp, mostly Mar 2020 and Jan–Feb 2026) the curve bends, and part of that bend lands in the residuals.
- **Residuals are on the daily close** (last half-hour VWAP). They are not fills.
- **Contracts before the first spec PDF we hold** (before 2025 for GOLDGUINEA and GOLDPETAL) use an assumed 999 purity. If pre-2025 GOLDPETAL was quoted at 995, its 2021–24 residual moves by about +40 bp. That would still leave it at −10 to −104 bp, so the regime break stands.
